- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 1.00 to 0.00 or vice versa), model reacts with lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); model often misses reversion; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias if sentiment is flat.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00/0.00 extremes, model overfits to recent extremes; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast.
